title_en: Michael Ervolini on Separating Skill From Luck
title_zh: Michael Ervolini 谈如何区分投资中的实力与运气
description: Selecting active managers has always been one of investing’s greatest challenges, in part because strong performance doesn’t always reflect repeatable skill. In this episode of Inside Active, host David Cohne, mutual fund and active management analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence, speaks with Michael Ervolini, author of “Skill Versus Luck,” about why investors should rethink how they evaluate active managers. They discuss the limitations of traditional performance metrics, how decision-based analytics can help separate skill from luck, and why analyzing buying, selling and position-sizing decisions may offer deeper insight into manager ability. They also explore the role of investment process, behavioral biases, AI and whether better skill measurement can improve manager selection and alter the balance between active and passive investing. Recorded July 16.

turns.en: Welcome to Inside Active, a podcast about active managers that goes beyond sound bites and headlines and looks deeper into their processes, challenges, and philosophies and security selection. I'm David cone I, lead mutual fund and active Research at Bloomberg Intelligence. Selecting active managers has been one of the biggest challenges in investing. While performance, risk, attribution, and other portfolio metrics can tell us how fun performed, they don't necessarily tell us whether that performance was the result of repeatable skill or simply favorable market conditions. For institutional investors, consultants, and financial advisors, separating genuine investment skill from luck remains one of the industry's most difficult and most important questions. Recent advances in portfolio analytics are challenging some long held assumption about how active managers should be evaluated. Rather than focusing primarily on investment outcomes, a growing body of research suggests investors may gain deeper insights by examining the decision makers, what they buy, what they sell, how they seize positions, and how consistently those decisions add value over time. So today I wanted to explore how investors should think about measuring manager's skill, why traditional performance metrics may not tell the full story, and whether a more decision based approach could improve active manager selection. So join me to discuss that is Michael Ervolini, author of Skill Versus Luck taking the guests out of Equity fund selection. Mike, thanks for joining me today.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 Inside Active，这是一档聚焦主动管理人（active manager）的播客。我们不止于只言片语和新闻标题，而是深入探讨他们的投资流程（investment process）、挑战、投资理念（investment philosophy）和证券选择（security selection）。我是 David Cohne，负责 Bloomberg Intelligence 的共同基金（mutual fund）与主动管理研究。选择主动管理人一直是投资领域最大的挑战之一。业绩、风险、归因和其他投资组合指标可以告诉我们基金表现如何，但不一定能告诉我们，这些表现究竟源于可重复的技能，还是仅仅得益于有利的市场环境。对于机构投资者、顾问和财务顾问而言，将真正的投资技能与运气区分开来，仍是行业中最困难、也最重要的问题之一。投资组合分析的最新进展，正对一些长期以来关于如何评估主动管理人的假设提出挑战。越来越多的研究表明，与主要关注投资结果相比，投资者通过考察决策本身，或许能获得更深入的洞察：管理人买什么、卖什么、如何确定仓位规模（position sizing），以及这些决策能否持续地创造价值。因此，今天我想探讨投资者应如何思考管理人技能的衡量，传统业绩指标为何可能无法呈现全貌，以及一种更注重决策的方法能否改善主动管理人的遴选。今天与我一同讨论的是 Michael Ervolini，他是《Skill Versus Luck: Taking the Guesswork Out of Equity Fund Selection》一书的作者。Mike，感谢你今天参加节目。

turns.en: It's a pleasure, David, and I appreciate the opportunity to speak with you and your audience great.
turns.zh: David，很高兴参加节目，也感谢你给我机会与听众交流。

turns.en: So what problem were you trying to solve when you wrote this book Skill Versus Luck?
turns.zh: 很好。你写《Skill Versus Luck》这本书时，试图解决什么问题？

turns.en: Fundamentally, it was helping the industry overcome conventional thinking. It's a challenge in every industry trying to move forward rather than holding fast to the current activities and beliefs we have. And as you mentioned in your intro, there's quite a few activities going on right now where people are using decision based analytics to give better insights into manager skill. That area hasn't received as much traction as it needs, and so in writing the book, I was hoping to stimulate an industry wide conversation about why we need to go beyond outcome based analytics and look at decision based analytics in combination so that people can get a deeper and richer understanding of what skills are driving the fund results, what skills are persistent, and all of that can allow investors to be more confident in selecting managers that have a greater likelihood of outperforming in the future. And really that's what cation decisions are all about, is who you want to give your money to in order to get better returns going forward.
turns.zh: 从根本上说，是帮助行业突破传统思维。在每个行业里，推动进步而不是固守现有做法和观念，都是一项挑战。正如你在开场时提到的，目前已有不少人在使用基于决策的分析，更深入地洞察管理人的技能。这个领域获得的关注还远远不够。因此，我写这本书，是希望推动一场全行业的讨论：为什么我们需要超越基于结果的分析，将其与基于决策的分析结合起来，让人们更深入、更全面地理解，究竟哪些技能推动了基金业绩，哪些技能具有持续性。所有这些都能让投资者在选择管理人时更有信心，因为这些管理人未来跑赢市场的可能性更高。资产配置决策归根结底就是：为了在未来获得更好的回报，你愿意把钱交给谁。

turns.en: So you're the title of the book kind of suggests we consistently are constantly confused luck with skill. Why do you think intelligent people make that mistake so often?
turns.zh: 书名似乎表明，我们总是在把运气和技能混为一谈。你认为，聪明人为什么如此频繁地犯这种错误？

turns.en: Well, two points on that one is I really believe that skill and luck are just opposite ends of a continuum, and so when a fund manager has more skill, they're less dependent upon luck for their results. So that's part one is skill and luck are involved in every decision. You just want managers that are more skilled. But a more specific answer to your question is, when you're making decisions using conventional analytics, they bring you to the threshold of understanding skill, but then you need to make a jump. You need to overinterpret the results or see in them something that you want to see. In other words, you have to guess a little bit. And I think because of that inadequacy of conventional analytics at addressing skill it makes it hard to figure out which managers are skilled and which aren't, and that has been plaguing the industry for a while. It continues to do so. But I have worked with institutional investors in particular who've been using decision based analytics, and their ability to sort out superior managers has improved as a result of this. So we can get past this. But most of the confusion has to do with working with inferior analytics as opposed to people not trying their best.
turns.zh: 这涉及两点。第一，我确实认为，技能和运气只是同一连续谱的两端。基金经理的技能越强，其业绩对运气的依赖就越少。所以第一点是，每个决策中都既有技能，也有运气；你只是希望管理人的技能更强。更具体地回答你的问题：当你使用传统分析做决策时，它们只能把你带到理解技能的门槛，接下来你还得自己跨过去。你必须过度解读结果，或者从中看到自己想看到的东西。换句话说，你不得不做一些猜测。我认为，正是因为传统分析不足以评估技能，人们才很难判断哪些管理人真正有技能、哪些没有。这一问题困扰行业已经有一段时间，而且仍在继续。不过，我曾与一些机构投资者合作，尤其是那些使用基于决策分析的机构；结果表明，他们筛选出优秀管理人的能力因此得到了提升。所以，我们能够克服这个问题。多数困惑来自使用了较为低效的分析方法，而不是因为人们没有尽力。

turns.en: So do you think we're kind of wired to judge outcomes rather than decisions.
turns.zh: 那么，你是否认为，我们天生更倾向于根据结果而不是决策来作判断？

turns.en: Yeah. One of the confusions that we have is how we make decisions. And what is not commonly understood is that more than ninety five percent the decisions we make every day are made completely automatically by our unconscious and so a lot of what's happening, whether it's a buying a stock, picking a manager, or ordering something off the menu, these automatic decisions generally work. But they only work really well where there's been great feedback about how good the decision is and how good the outcome has been. And so in that automatic decision environment. When you're using outcome based analytics, you see in them what you want, and so I think when asset owners or allocators are shown decision based results against outcome based results, they can take the best of both. But lacking any kind of decision based analytics and using only outcome based analytics, our natural instinct is to see in those results something that seems reason and often what we see is completely wrong.
turns.zh: 是的。我们对自己如何作出决策存在一些误解。一个并不广为人知的事实是，我们每天作出的决策中，超过 95% 都完全由无意识自动完成。所以，无论是买股票、选择管理人，还是照着菜单点餐，这些自动决策通常都能奏效。但只有在我们获得了充分反馈，知道决策有多好、结果有多好时，它们才会真正发挥出色。在这种自动决策的环境中，当你使用基于结果的分析时，你会从中看到自己想看到的东西。因此，我认为，当资产所有者或资产配置者同时看到基于决策和基于结果的分析结果时，他们可以兼取两者之长。但如果完全缺乏基于决策的分析，只使用基于结果的分析，我们的本能就会让我们从结果中看出某种似乎合乎情理的解释，而我们看到的东西往往完全错误。

turns.en: Okay, and you know you redefine skill as the combined effect of expert judgment and investment processes. Why did you feel the industry needed a new definition?
turns.zh: 好的。你把技能重新定义为专家判断和投资流程的综合作用。为什么你认为行业需要一个新的定义？

turns.en: Well, I think partly is because we had been looking at skill the wrong way. We've been looking at it as outcomes, and when you look at that, it's hard to figure out what's in there. So if we're going to look at decisions, then we want to focus on what is it the manager brings to the fund and the manager brings to qualities, their expert judgment and their investment process, and that's what they should be judged on. And fortunately, decision based analytics can allow you to rigorously evaluate and quantify both of those elements judgment and process, and when you understand them well you can then get a sense of how consistently good the men is making buying, selling, sizing decisions, and using that, I think what we've seen in the industry is that people then have more confidence that the manager they're working with, well not perfect, has a better than average chance about performing going forward.
turns.zh: 部分原因是，我们过去看待技能的方式不对。我们一直把技能当成结果来看，而当你只看结果时，很难判断其中究竟包含什么。因此，如果我们要看决策，就应该聚焦于管理人为基金带来了什么。管理人带来了两项特质：专家判断和投资流程；他们就应该依据这两项特质接受评估。幸运的是，基于决策的分析可以让你严谨地评估和量化判断与流程这两个要素。充分理解它们之后，你就能判断管理人在买入、卖出和仓位规模管理方面作出优质决策的稳定程度。我认为，行业经验表明，借助这种方法，人们会更加相信，与自己合作的管理人虽然并不完美，但未来跑赢市场的概率高于平均水平。

turns.en: So then how do you actually separate you know, a good decision from a lucky outcome, Like, how do you go in and do that?
turns.zh: 那么，你究竟如何区分一个好决策和一个幸运的结果？具体是怎么做的？

turns.en: Well, there's always going to be some luck. Okay, that's just we'll call that the market.
turns.zh: 运气始终会占一部分。好吧，我们就把这部分称为市场因素。

turns.en: You know, if you were.
turns.zh: 比如说，如果你……

turns.en: Lucky enough to buy the Magnificent seven some years ago and overweight them extensively, part of that was a good decision, and part of that is they've just done remarkably well. So there's a little bit of luck, or if your style is in favor and so forth. But given that we can look at individual decisions, let's say a buying decision. What we can do is over a period of time, we use ten years just for easy number. We look at every position that was purchased over that ten year period, and then we evaluate, independently from how the manager sized a position or when they sold it, on average, how did those positions do in aggregate that they generate excess return or not on their own. And so we can do that for sizing, we can do that for adding on the way up, adding on the way down. We can look at decisions broadly or very very narrowly, and the idea is to isolate individual types of decisions and evaluate if they, on average are helping to generate more excess return or in fact are taking away excess return, which is obviously a negative skill.
turns.zh: 如果你足够幸运，在几年前买入了“科技七巨头”（Magnificent Seven），并大幅超配，其中一部分源于好的决策，另一部分则是因为它们的表现确实异常出色。所以这里面会有一点运气；又比如，你的投资风格恰好受到市场青睐，等等。但既然我们可以考察单个决策，那就以买入决策为例。在一段时间内——为了便于说明，我们就用 10 年——我们查看这 10 年间买入的每一个仓位，然后在排除管理人如何确定仓位规模以及何时卖出的影响后，评估这些仓位整体而言平均表现如何：仅靠这些买入本身，它们是否产生了超额收益。我们也可以用同样的方法评估仓位规模管理，评估上涨途中加仓和下跌途中加仓。我们既可以非常宽泛，也可以非常细致地考察决策。核心思路是把不同类型的决策逐一分离出来，评估它们平均而言是在帮助创造更多超额收益，还是实际上削减了超额收益；后一种情况显然就是负向技能。

turns.en: Okay, and you know, one of the most interesting concepts I think in the book is the counterfactual portfolio. Can you kind of explain that idea and plan English.
turns.zh: 好的。我认为，书中最有意思的概念之一是反事实投资组合。你能用通俗易懂的语言解释一下这个概念吗？

turns.en: Sure, a counterfactual portfolio is simply a copy of the actual portfolio, but then one decision type is adjusted to understand its impact on the portfolio. So a very straightforward example is this, there's a fund where the manager periodically purchases stocks that are outside the benchmark of the fund, and presumably these out of benchmark purchases are intended to generate excess return or alpha. Well, one way to evaluate that is to create a copy of the fund and then go through it every day, and whenever the manager buys a position that's outside the benchmark. Just simply eliminate that from the copy or the counterfactual. And so when you're done doing that exercise, the counterfactual portfolio on every single day owns exactly what's in the actual portfolio, except it doesn't own any out of benchmark positions. And now with that counterfactual portfolio, you generate its returns and its excess return. You can do information ratios, whatever metrics you want, and compare those to the actual. Now, if we're looking at relative return, if the actual portfolio has a higher relative return than the counterfactual, that tells us owning those out of benchmark positions really helped it generated more excess return. Conversely, if the actual portfolio underperforms the counterfactual, it tells us that owning those out of benchmark positions actually hurt the results. So that's the idea of a counterfactual. You take one decision type at a time, you either eliminate it or alter it, and then compare it back to the actual and that way you're able to see whether specific decisions are additive or detracting from overall success in the fund.
turns.zh: 当然。反事实投资组合就是实际投资组合的一个副本，但会调整其中一种决策，以了解该决策对投资组合的影响。一个非常直观的例子是：某只基金的管理人会定期买入基金业绩基准（benchmark）之外的股票。按理说，买入这些基准外股票是为了创造超额收益（alpha）。一种评估方法是复制这只基金，然后每天检查这个副本；每当管理人买入一个基准外仓位时，就直接从这个副本，也就是反事实投资组合中剔除该仓位。完成这项工作后，在每一个交易日，反事实投资组合所持有的资产都与实际投资组合完全一致，唯一的区别是它不持有任何基准外仓位。接下来，你就可以计算这个反事实投资组合的收益和超额收益，也可以计算信息比率或任何你想使用的指标，再把这些结果与实际投资组合比较。如果我们考察相对收益（relative return），而实际投资组合的相对收益高于反事实投资组合，这就说明持有那些基准外仓位确实有所帮助，创造了更多超额收益。反过来，如果实际投资组合跑输反事实投资组合，就说明持有那些基准外仓位实际上损害了业绩。这就是反事实投资组合的思路：每次选取一种决策，剔除或改变它，然后与实际投资组合进行比较。这样，你就能判断具体决策是提升了基金的整体成效，还是对其造成了拖累。

turns.en: Now it makes sense, it makes a lot of sense. It's really interesting. You know. I also couldn't help but think that, you know, what you're looking at applies even beyond investing. Do you think your framework could be used to evaluate, you know, even CEOs or even sports coaches.
turns.zh: 明白了，很有道理。这真的很有意思。我还不禁想到，你考察的这些内容甚至适用于投资领域之外。你认为，这套框架能否用来评估首席执行官，甚至体育教练？

turns.en: I'm not sure I've thought about that. It's possible. It definitely was meant to be used across any publicly treated asset type, that's for sure, so option swaps, fixed income. But beyond that, we've never tackled anything like that, So I'm not sure it's possible, But I'm not sure.
turns.zh: 我不确定自己是否想过这个问题。有这种可能。可以确定的是，这套框架原本就是为各种公开交易的资产类别设计的，包括期权（option）、掉期和固定收益（fixed income）。但除此之外，我们从未处理过类似问题，所以我不确定是否可行。确实不确定。

turns.en: It's definitely interesting concept. And you know, obviously the biggest, you know, one of the biggest criticisms you've had is allocators spend way too much time evaluating performance, not enough time evaluating decisions. If you were sitting on an investment community today, what would you stop measuring and what would you start measuring?
turns.zh: 这绝对是个有意思的概念。显然，你提出的一个主要批评是，资产配置者花了太多时间评估业绩，却没有投入足够时间评估决策。如果你今天是投资委员会的一员，你会停止衡量什么，又会开始衡量什么？

turns.en: Well, I'm not sure I would stop measuring anything, but I would add a whole lot of decision based analytics. I would want to know how effective the manager is at buying, selling, and sizing, and then I would want to look at them from multiple perspectives. I would want to look, let's say, ten years again, how good was buying over ten years, how good was it year by year to see how consistent it was, How good is the buying across sectors, to make sure that we're not just leaning on a few sectors, but the manager's good across the board. And I might want to look at it by factor. If there's a certain element in the strategy that the managers expressing in their coversations or their marketing material about we look for stocks with these characteristics, I would want to use those factors to evaluate the buying as well. As an example, if the manager says they'd like to buy high quality companies, well, we could use any number of factors to evaluate the quality of a company balance sheet, debt, or whatever we want to do and see if in fact, higher quality balance sheet companies show up as being the stronger buys in the portfolio. So I'd want to do a lot of work like that, And when you get to that place, you know that the manager is doing what they said they're going to do, They're doing it very well every year and over time, it's really adding value to the fund. That, in combination with conventional analytics, allows you to know that over the past few years the results have been great too. The amount of risk taking was not disproportional to the return, and they're well within their peer group, and all that kind of stuff. All these conventional analytics are important, they simply don't provide enough information about skill.
turns.zh: 我不确定自己会停止衡量任何东西，但我会增加大量基于决策的分析。我想知道管理人在买入、卖出和仓位规模管理方面的成效，然后从多个角度考察。比如，我们还是看 10 年：这 10 年间的买入水平如何？逐年看又如何，以判断其稳定性？各个行业的买入水平如何，以确保我们不是只依赖少数几个行业，而是管理人在各领域都表现出色？我可能还会按因子来考察。如果管理人在谈话或营销材料中称，策略中的某个要素是“我们寻找具备这些特征的股票”，我也会用这些因子来评估买入决策。举个例子，如果管理人说自己喜欢买入高质量公司，那么，我们可以使用许多不同因子来评估公司的资产负债表质量、债务或任何其他指标，看看资产负债表质量更高的公司是否确实是投资组合中表现更强的买入标的。我会做大量类似的工作。做到这一步后，你就能知道管理人是否言行一致，是否年复一年地把这件事做得很好，以及这是否确实长期为基金创造了价值。把这些分析与传统分析结合起来，你还能知道过去几年的业绩是否也很出色，所承担的风险相对于回报是否并不过高，以及他们在同业组中的位置是否合理，等等。所有这些传统分析都很重要，只是无法提供足够多的技能信息。

turns.en: Okay, you know you obviously spent decades looking at how professional investors make decisions. What do you think the biggest misconception people have about how decisions are actually made?
turns.zh: 好的。你显然花了几十年研究专业投资者如何作出决策。你认为，人们对决策实际形成方式最大的误解是什么？

turns.en: Well, I mentioned one, which is this unconscious bit thinking. Recognizing that most of your decisions are unconscious really convinces me and a lot of other people that it's imperative that you have a strong process because that can arrest some of the automatic decision making and make sure that you stay in the area where you make your best decisions. Another misconception is emotions. We hear frequently, at least I have in my career an investor or money manager or other profession I will say, well, we take all the emotions out of our decision making. We do everything here by the numbers. Well, that sounds great, but it's actually impossible. What neuroscience tells us is it's literally impossible to make a rational choice without emotions. You can add up a column of numbers without emotions because there's no judgment involved. You're just adding numbers. But when you're trying to make a choice, what discount rates to use? What fund am I ultimately going to pick for my allocation? What research am I going to use to help me get to that place? Those choices, you get to difficult spots where it's not easy to differentiate one option from another, and a little emotional spark is what helps in the tie breakers. And so understanding that your emotions play a role in your decision making is another reason you want to have a good process because it can slow you down and allow you to arrest. Automatic decision making allow you to harness emotions in a positive way. And when you embrace those two concepts and use them to help build your process, that result is you get much better decision making.
turns.zh: 我刚才提到过一个误解，就是无意识思维。意识到大多数决策都是无意识作出的，让我和许多人都深信，建立一套强有力的流程至关重要，因为它能抑制一部分自动决策，确保你待在自己最擅长作决策的领域。另一个误解与情绪有关。至少在我的职业生涯中，我经常听投资者、资产管理人（money manager）或其他专业人士说：“我们在决策中排除了一切情绪，这里的一切都以数字为依据。”这听起来很好，但实际上做不到。神经科学告诉我们，在没有情绪参与的情况下，人实际上不可能作出理性选择。你可以在不带情绪的情况下把一列数字相加，因为这里不涉及判断，你只是在做加法。但当你试图作出选择时——该使用什么折现率（discount rate）？最终该为资产配置选择哪只基金？该采用哪些研究来帮助我作出选择？——你会遇到难以抉择的时刻，不同选项之间很难区分，而一点点情绪火花会帮助你打破平局。因此，理解情绪会在决策中发挥作用，也是你需要良好流程的另一个原因：流程能让你放慢速度，抑制自动决策，并让你以积极方式利用情绪。当你接受这两个概念，并以此帮助构建流程时，结果就是你能作出好得多的决策。

turns.en: Do you think there's you know, a danger we've become obsessed with measuring everything, you know, in other words, can skill itself become over engineered.
turns.zh: 你认为，我们是否存在一种危险：变得痴迷于衡量一切？换句话说，技能本身会不会被过度工程化？

turns.en: I think we can overmeasure things. Yeah, we can lose sight of what we're really after. And if that happens, it's because we didn't have a good plan going in. You know, we have to understand why we're measuring skill and what we want to come out of it. But I will caution this frequently, the fear of overmeasurement can be used as an argument to hang onto convention, to not take a step forward to state where we are more comfortable in presenting these analytics. To some fund managers, sometimes the pushback is, well, you know, I don't want you coming in and messing up what I'm doing now. Well, so I don't want to see this stuff now. I think there's a little fear in there about learning what you do well and what you don't. So there's a balance point. Yes, we can't go overboard and measure too much or follow analytics too far, because no analytic is perfect. But reasonable people can take on new analytics and learn to make better decisions. And that's what it's all about. Being proportional, being reasonable and understanding that the purpose here is to make better decisions, not just to measure things or to follow analytics one hundred percent.
turns.zh: 我认为，我们确实可能过度衡量一些事情。我们可能会忘记自己真正追求的是什么。如果发生这种情况，那是因为我们一开始就没有制订好计划。我们必须理解为什么要衡量技能，以及希望从中得到什么。不过，我经常会提醒大家：对过度衡量的担忧，可能被用作固守传统的理由，让人们拒绝向前迈进，停留在自己更熟悉、更习惯展示的分析方法上。向一些基金经理展示这些分析时，他们有时会反驳说：“我不希望你进来把我现在做的事情搞乱。所以，我现在不想看这些东西。”我认为，这里面夹杂着一点恐惧，他们害怕了解自己擅长什么、不擅长什么。因此，需要找到平衡点。没错，我们不能做过头、衡量太多，也不能过度依赖分析，因为没有任何一种分析是完美的。但理性的人能够采用新的分析方法，并学会作出更好的决策。归根结底，关键就在于此：把握分寸、保持理性，并理解我们的目的在于作出更好的决策，而不只是衡量事物，或百分之百地照着分析结果行事。

turns.en: You know your approach depends on analyzing thousands of decisions. Could someone argue that investing is still too uncertain to isolate skill.
turns.zh: 你的方法依赖于分析数千个决策。是否有人会认为，投资的不确定性仍然太高，无法把技能单独分离出来？

turns.en: I don't think so now, because I myself have been involved in analyzing four or five six hundred funds, and there's no question that skill can be measured. And there are other companies out there that have collectively looked at perhaps eight or nine thousand funds, and so skill can be measured, can be isolated, can be quantified. It's done differently by different analytics shops, but there's no question that can be isolated. It simply can't be done using conventional analytics.
turns.zh: 现在我不这么认为，因为我本人已经参与分析过四五百只、甚至 600 只基金。毫无疑问，技能是可以衡量的。还有其他一些公司合计考察过大约 8,000 或 9,000 只基金。因此，技能可以衡量、可以分离，也可以量化。不同分析机构采用的方法各不相同，但毫无疑问，技能可以被分离出来。只是靠传统分析无法做到这一点。

turns.en: Okay, you know Warren Buffett has said that you know, temperament matters more than IQ. Does your framework capture qualities like patients, discipline, conviction or is it only you know, kind of measurable decisions.
turns.zh: 好的。Warren Buffett 曾说，性情比智商更重要。你的框架能否捕捉耐心、纪律、投资确信度（conviction）之类的特质，还是只能捕捉可衡量的决策？

turns.en: No, In fact, it can help you determine some of those things. One example, let's say patients. Okay, we could look at when a manager is buys stocks and they take off relatively early after purchase. Does the manager hang on to them or does the manager sell them far too quickly and give up a lot of alpha. Now there's a patience issue. So by looking at new winners and evaluating whether they're being sold too quickly or not, that's a way of getting into patients conviction. We can look at when positions are purchased and maybe in the first few months they take a dip in price. Sometimes an early dip in price is an indication that the manager bought a bad stock. Other times it's just that the market has had a bad reaction to that company, but the fundamentals really haven't changed, and more often than not, those stocks are going to bounce back. And by evaluating that behavior, we can see whether the manager has sufficient conviction in stocks that wiggle a little bit right after they're purchased, but ultimately do really, really well. So we can look for behavioral kinds of aspects in the manager looking at the decisions they make.
turns.zh: 不，事实上，它能帮助你识别其中一些特质。比如耐心。假设一位管理人买入股票后，这些股票很快就开始上涨。管理人会继续持有，还是过早卖出，从而放弃大量超额收益？这就涉及耐心问题。因此，通过观察新近出现的赢家，并评估它们是否被过早卖出，我们就能考察耐心。至于投资确信度，我们可以观察仓位建立后最初几个月内价格是否有所下跌。有时，买入后不久价格下跌，说明管理人买错了股票；另一些时候，只是市场对这家公司作出了负面反应，但基本面其实没有变化，而这些股票往往会反弹。通过评估这种行为，我们可以判断，当股票在买入后不久出现小幅波动、但最终表现非常出色时，管理人是否对它们保持了足够的投资确信度。所以，我们可以通过观察管理人作出的决策，寻找其行为层面的特征。

turns.en: Okay, you know another thing that you know kind of really jumped out was that you know you've concluded that buying is usually the biggest drive of alpha. Why do you think buying is more important than selling. Well, if you're not.
turns.zh: 好的。还有一点特别引人注意：你的结论是，买入通常是超额收益的最大驱动因素。为什么你认为买入比卖出更重要？

turns.en: A good buyer, you're basically starting out in a hole, and it's hard to sell your way out of a hole and generate alpha. It can be done, but it's really hard. But if you start out buying good stocks, you can have a few mistakes on sizing and selling and still do pretty well, so it's just a question of starting off on the strongest platform possible. And that's with good buying. In general speaking, most successful managers are really really good buyers. There's a few that are not, but and I can explain why if that's of interest, But generally speaking, they're good buyers.
turns.zh: 这个嘛，如果你不擅长买入，基本上从一开始就掉进了坑里；想只靠卖出来填平这个坑并创造超额收益，非常困难。并非完全做不到，但真的很难。但如果你一开始就买入了好股票，那么即使在仓位规模管理和卖出上犯几个错误，表现仍然可以相当不错。所以，问题只是要尽可能从最坚实的平台起步，而这个平台就是出色的买入。总体而言，大多数成功的管理人都非常、非常擅长买入。也有少数例外。如果你感兴趣，我可以解释原因。但总体上，他们都是出色的买家。

turns.en: So that kind of brings me to the next part is you know the you argue that selling is probably that the industry's weakest skill. You know, and when I speak to managers, I always I don't want to know just what their buying philosophy is, but you know what makes them sell? And so what do you think a lot of professionals struggle so much? Was selling?
turns.zh: 这正好引出下一个问题。你认为，卖出可能是整个行业最薄弱的技能。我与管理人交谈时，不只想了解他们的买入理念，也总想知道什么因素会促使他们卖出。那么，你认为为什么许多专业人士在卖出方面如此吃力？

turns.en: It's the least understood. If you were to do a quick search on equity investing strategy, everything you.
turns.zh: 因为它最不为人理解。如果你快速搜索一下股票投资策略，你……

turns.en: Found would be about buying.
turns.zh: 找到的所有内容都会与买入有关。

turns.en: When it so that's the whole industry in academy itself, when they think about the strategic decisions inside of equity investing or any other asset class, it's generally they're looking at buying. Selling is often a discipline. Well, if buying is strategic and selling is a discipline, it sort of tells you that selling is sort of the orphan of thinking in asset management, and so it's not well understood. The second thing is what is a good sell. Often people believe that a good sell is after I sell the stock the price goes down. Well, that's not necessarily a good description. A better one is A good sell is when you sell a stock and after you sell it, its return is less than the fund's average. So, in other words, you want to hang onto stocks that can lift up the fund average return, and you want to sell stocks that will take down the fund's average return, meaning that if the market is going down, holding onto a stock that only goes down five percent when a lot of other stocks are going down ten percent, well you shouldn't sell that stock even though it's priced going down. So we get confused a little bit about what a good sell is. And again it's selling a stock before it drags down the average. That's the fundamental test. And then the fact that academia and other analytics really don't look at selling particularly well. Conventional analytics are really nonexistent in their ability to help you understand selling. The decision based analytics do a real nice job at looking at selling selling when stocks are up selling when stocks are down. You can look at selling all different manners and really understand it. But most managers do not have good analytics to help them understand their selling, and that's why they try their best, but they really can't improve it because they don't have the right feedback.
turns.zh: 正是如此。整个行业乃至学术界，在思考股票投资或任何其他资产类别中的战略决策时，通常关注的都是买入。卖出往往只被视为一种纪律。如果买入是战略，而卖出只是纪律，这某种程度上说明，在资产管理的思考体系中，卖出像是一个无人照管的孤儿，因此没有得到充分理解。第二个问题是，什么才算好的卖出？人们常常认为，好的卖出就是我卖出股票后，股价下跌。但这并不一定是恰当的定义。更好的定义是：当你卖出一只股票后，它的收益低于基金平均收益，这才是好的卖出。换句话说，你希望持有能够抬高基金平均收益的股票，卖出会拉低基金平均收益的股票。也就是说，如果市场正在下跌，许多其他股票都下跌 10%，而你持有的一只股票只下跌 5%，那么即便它的价格也在下跌，你也不应该卖掉它。因此，人们对于什么是好的卖出存在一些误解。再强调一次，根本标准是在一只股票拖累平均收益之前将其卖出。此外，学术界和其他分析方法其实并不擅长研究卖出。传统分析几乎完全无法帮助你理解卖出。基于决策的分析则非常擅长考察卖出：股票上涨时卖出、股票下跌时卖出，以及各种不同情况下的卖出，都能得到分析和真正的理解。但大多数管理人都没有好的分析工具来帮助自己理解卖出决策。这就是为什么他们虽然尽了最大努力，却仍然无法改进，因为他们没有得到正确的反馈。

turns.en: Okay, and you know, if you had to pick one investment habit, you know you think every active manager should stop doing tomorrow. What do you think that would be?
turns.zh: 好的。如果必须选出一种你认为每位主动管理人从明天起都应该停止的投资习惯，你会选什么？

turns.en: Reaching for conviction too quickly? Conviction is an important element. When you talk to managers, they talk about it. When consultants took the managers, they ask them about their conviction. Conviction is a well bandeed word in the industry and it's important.
turns.zh: 过快形成投资确信度。投资确信度是一个重要要素。与管理人交谈时，他们会谈到它；顾问与管理人交谈时，也会询问他们的投资确信度。“投资确信度”是行业中广为使用的词，也确实很重要。

turns.en: But what the.
turns.zh: 但研究……

turns.en: Research shows is coming to it slowly and allowing it to develop, particularly using your analysts, using the investment committee, using your research team. Allowing conviction to develop slowly allows the manager to be more confident that they're really dealing with well airned conviction and not just bluster. And telling the difference when you're excited is really really hard. So that again brings me back to why process is so important. Getting to a discipline process where you can let your unconscious do its best job. Let your emotions help you as much as they can, but let others in your organization offer questions, criticism, or support. All of that allows the manager to develop real fiction and make their best decisions.
turns.zh: 但研究表明，应该缓慢形成投资确信度，给它时间逐步发展，尤其是要借助你的分析师、投资委员会和研究团队。让投资确信度缓慢发展，能使管理人更有把握，确认自己真正拥有的是充分论证后形成的投资确信度，而不只是虚张声势。当你情绪高涨时，要分辨二者真的非常困难。所以，这又让我回到流程为何如此重要。建立一套严谨的流程，让你的无意识发挥最佳作用，让情绪尽可能帮助你，同时让组织中的其他人提出问题、批评或支持。所有这些都有助于管理人形成真正的投资确信度，并作出最好的决策。

turns.en: Okay, you know we're obviously entering an error where AI can analyze enormous amounts of information. Do you think AI makes skill more valuable or less valuable?
turns.zh: 好的。我们显然正进入一个人工智能（artificial intelligence, AI）能够分析海量信息的时代。你认为，AI 会让技能变得更有价值，还是更没有价值？

turns.en: Right now? There's no question it makes skill more valuable. There's a recent research report from Lauren Cohen out of Harvard just came out in the past seven or ten days where they use some large language models to mimic a number of mutual funds over an extended period of time, and what they found out is that these largers language models were really really good at anticipating something between seventy five and eighty percent of the stocks that the fund actually purchased over time. What they also found is that the stock the large language models didn't buy were the ones that contained most of the alpha. So there's something about human judgment at the edge of the marketplace that is pretty impressive today. It allows people to really do some spectacular stuff. Will that always be the case, I don't know, but my sense is markets move so fast, humans are always going to have a role to play. One other supporting piece of evidence I can offer is back in the Great Crash and eight nine, I remember being at a conference of chief investment officers and some of the risk managers, global risk managers, and what they were saying is, at that moment they abandoned their models because they weren't trained on such an extreme situation. So to the extent things move rapidly and we see extreme activities going on, I think humans are going to be a little bit smarter because they can see and pull things together a little faster today. Again, who knows what's going to happen years to come, But right now there's some evidence that AI can make humans do even better. It's not clear that they can supplant them completely.
turns.zh: 就目前而言，毫无疑问，它让技能变得更有价值。Harvard 的 Lauren Cohen 最近发布了一份研究报告，就在过去 7 天或 10 天内。研究人员使用一些大语言模型，在相当长的一段时间里模拟多只共同基金。他们发现，这些大语言模型确实非常擅长预测基金随后会买入哪些股票，预测准确率在 75% 到 80% 之间。他们还发现，大语言模型没有买入的那些股票，恰恰贡献了大部分超额收益。所以，在市场前沿，人类判断中有某种东西直到今天仍令人印象深刻，它能让人们作出一些非常出色的决策。这种情况是否会一直持续？我不知道。但我的感觉是，市场变化如此之快，人类始终会扮演一定角色。我还可以提供另一项佐证。回想 2008—2009 年金融危机期间，我曾参加一场首席投资官会议，一些风险经理和全球风险经理表示，在当时那个节点，他们放弃了自己的模型，因为那些模型从未针对如此极端的情况接受训练。因此，只要形势变化迅速、极端事件不断出现，我认为人类就会稍微聪明一些，因为就目前而言，人类能更快地观察并整合各种信息。再说一次，谁知道未来几年会发生什么？但目前已有一些证据表明，AI 能帮助人类做得更好；至于 AI 能否彻底取代人类，尚无定论。

turns.en: Okay, And kind of on that note or a little bit, you know, kind of going away from AI. But you know, if we talk about ten years from now, if you rewrote this book in ten years, what do you think would change.
turns.zh: 好的。顺着这个话题——或者稍微离开 AI 一点——假设来到 10 年后，如果那时你重写这本书，你认为会有哪些变化？

turns.en: Well, my challenge, as I said earlier, is to overcome convention. So what would be great to be able to write is that overcoming convention was not as hard and didn't take as long as I originally thought that would be a great thing to be able to write ten years. No, that's my hope. I also think we'll see, without question, a more greater adoption of decision based analytics, and I think we will see a lot more AI being used in the industry, and hopefully we'll see the opportunity for active management to become stronger, and we may find a different balance point between active and passive investing. Right now, I think there's such a challenge in identifying a skilled manager that many investors are choosing to allocate more capital passively simply because they're afraid of picking the wrong manager. But if we can make skill as transparent as it needs to be and as it can be, then I think that offers the opportunity for a different balance point between active and passive, and that's another benefit we get by going down this road of improving our skilled metrics.
turns.zh: 正如我之前所说，我面临的挑战是突破传统观念。因此，如果 10 年后我能写道，突破传统并没有我起初想象的那么困难，也没有花那么长时间，那会是一件很棒的事。这是我的希望。我还认为，毫无疑问，我们会看到基于决策的分析得到更广泛的市场采用（adoption），行业中也会更多地使用 AI。希望我们能看到主动管理（active management）变得更强的机会，并可能在主动管理与被动投资（passive investing）之间找到一个不同的平衡点。目前，我认为识别有技能的管理人实在太难，以至于许多投资者选择把更多资本配置到被动投资，只因为他们害怕选错管理人。但如果我们能让技能达到其应有、也能够达到的透明度，那么，我认为这将带来机会，让主动管理与被动投资之间形成不同的平衡。这也是我们沿着改善技能衡量指标这条路走下去能够获得的另一项益处。

turns.en: Okay, I've got just one more question before I let you go. Every investor listening right now, remember just one idea from skill versus luck. What would you hope it would be that.
turns.zh: 好的。在结束之前，我还有最后一个问题。如果现在正在收听节目的每位投资者只能记住《Skill Versus Luck》中的一个观点，你希望那是什么？

turns.en: There are skilled managers out there. There are plenty of them, the difficulty is finding them. So whether you're an institutional investor, a manager search consultant, or an individual, what it's incumbent upon you to do is to begin to demand better skill metrics from whomever you work with, whether it's an internal team, if you're a pension fund, or whether it's a manager search firm, if you're a large investor, or if you're an individual, whatever platform you're using, start demanding better skill metrics. They exist, they're relatively inexpensive, and they add tremendously to your ability to make better allocation decisions. And what we're all trying to do is meet some financial need in the future, whether it's retirement or an endowment, or making investments in the community or in healthcare or whatever it is. The better we do with our investments, the better off we all are. And asking and demanding for better skill analytics can allow you to make better investment decisions. And that's certainly what I would be pushing for right now, is we need to change the industry. And it starts by saying, hey, why don't we have some different skill metrics on this platform.
turns.zh: 市场上确实存在有技能的管理人，而且数量很多，难点在于找到他们。因此，无论你是机构投资者、管理人筛选顾问，还是个人投资者，你都有责任开始要求与你合作的对象提供更好的技能衡量指标。对于养老基金而言，对方可能是内部团队；对于大型投资者而言，可能是管理人筛选公司；对于个人而言，则是你所使用的任何平台。开始要求更好的技能衡量指标吧。这些指标已经存在，成本相对不高，而且能极大提升你作出更好资产配置决策的能力。我们所有人努力的目标，都是满足未来的某种财务需求：可能是退休，可能是捐赠基金，也可能是投资社区、医疗健康或其他领域。我们的投资做得越好，所有人的处境就越好。要求并坚持获得更好的技能分析，能帮助你作出更好的投资决策。这无疑是我现在会大力推动的事情：我们需要改变这个行业。改变始于提出这样一个问题：“嘿，为什么我们正在使用的这个平台上，没有一些不同的技能衡量指标？”
